title: Annotatio IV §.XX: Taborite ‘with/in bread’ formulas seem Lutheran In/Cum/Sub — but Hoc is bread only
pass_a_gloss: Indeed for the Consensus of the Younger Waldenses with the Lutherans on the point of the Sacred Supper there could be introduced the Taborites’ first Article against the Prague Papists on the presence and adoration of Christ in the Sacrament — noted by neither of the pair of Theologians in their Dissertations — by which they expressly affirm: With the bread truly to be the body of Christ taken from the Virgin and handed over for us. Likewise: Christ’s Body to be in the bread: Which two formulas of speaking answer exactly to the Lutheran In, Cum, and Sub. But (1) In the same article the Taborites contend that the pronoun This in Christ’s proposition This is my Body demonstrates nothing other than the bread — which is altogether alien from the mind of modern Lutherans.
pass_b_english: A Taborite article neither Danhauer nor Strauch noted could seem to serve junior-Waldenses–Lutheran consensus: ‘with the bread truly Christ’s body’ and ‘Christ’s body in the bread’ — formulas matching Lutheran In, Cum, and Sub.
But (1) in the same article the Taborites make Hoc in ‘This is my Body’ point to nothing but the bread — wholly alien to the modern Lutheran mind.
source_text: Equidem pro Consensu Waldensium Juniorum cum Lutheranis in puncto de S. Cœna, introduci posset, Articulus primus Taboritarum contra Papistas Pragenses de præsentia & adoratione Christi in Sacramento, à neutro licet Theologorum binorum, in Dissertationibus eorum notatus, quô expressè perhibent: Cum pane verè esse corpus Christi de Virgine sumtum pro nobis traditum. Item: Corpus Christi in pane esse: Quæ duæ formulæ dicendi exactè respondent tô In, Cum, & Sub Lutherano. At (1) In eodem articulo contendunt Taboritæ, pronomen, Hoc, in propositione Christi: hoc est Corpus meum, aliud nihil, quàm panem demonstrare, id quod à mente Lutheranorum modernorum omnino alienum est.
